elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Revised 2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment..." — the USD 2,000,000/year three-year take-or-pay obligation is fully deleted, and no other clause imposes a volume floor or usage cap (7.1 in fact bars unidentified minimum-use charges).

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Revised 2.1: "...and will pay only for Services used or ordered during the applicable term," consistent with 7.1 (Fees stated in each Order Form; no unidentified minimum-use charge).

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: after the edit there is no purchase commitment at all, so there is nothing to limit to a 12-month term. The preferred outcome subsumes this fallback term.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no commitment survives in revised 2.1, so no reduction mechanic is needed; Customer's exposure is limited to Services actually used or ordered.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: the take-or-pay/shortfall mechanic in original 2.1 is deleted entirely, leaving no shortfall formula, instalment, or penalty to convert into a true-up.

reasons: Original 2.1 was walk-away territory: multi-year (three years) USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights" — no 12-month limit, no reduction on notice, no true-up, so it failed the fallback on every material term. "Deviation" is the correct status.

Both preferred elements are met in operative language by the single replacement of 2.1; no commitment, cap, shortfall, or minimum-use mechanic remains anywhere (7.1 independently bars unidentified minimum-use charges).

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the one offending sentence, is a concise substitution rather than an expansion, and adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure, remedy, or other extra outside the MINCOMMIT checklist. The retained 7.1 and 12.3 language, both Customer-favourable, is untouched.

Intent is preserved and internal consistency improved: the revision removes the direct contradiction with 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer "has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment," and leaves 7.1's Order-Form fee mechanic, fixed-fee protection, and usage-based unit-price carve-out operating without conflict. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("Services" and "term" remain defined/used as elsewhere).
No action required by the drafter; the comment correctly cites the preferred position and offers the 12-month/30-day/true-up fallback without conceding it in the operative text.
